aliases: Voice or music reference for a clip
feature.summary: Video-generation studio does not let a person pick a frame rate or supply reference audio on any app. The generate request has no field for either. The only audio control the server accepts is a yes/no generate_audio flag, and no client sends it. Both items are missing everywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person choose a clip's frame rate (where a video model supports it) and attach reference audio (a voice or music track) that guides the clip's sound. Today neither exists. The server accepts only prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, a generate_audio flag, provider, model, candidate count and image inputs (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:193-217).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists both as parts of a complete video studio: S46.09 (frame rate where the model supports it) and S46.14 (reference audio where supported) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md). Competitor guidance tells engineers to inspect audio behaviour and references in video workflows (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md section 5.17, item 132).
purpose.who_uses_it: People making short clips in the Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome video modes who want smoother or cinematic motion, or a specific voice or soundtrack. CLI and VS Code have no video mode, so they do not apply (brief status n/a).
problems_solved: Today: none, because the feature is not built.
If built: a person could match a clip's motion rate to their project and keep a consistent voice or music across clips.
use_cases: Pick 24 or 30 frames per second for a social clip (not possible today).
Attach a narration voice sample so the generated characters speak in that voice (not possible today).
Attach a music track as the mood reference for a clip (not possible today).

where_to_find_it: Not available on Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome. The Web video controls are the video model menu, 'Select video aspect ratio', 'Select video quality' and 'Select video length', with no frame-rate or audio control (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6561, :6614, :6668, :6857).

Mobile 'Create video' sheet offers 'Video model' and aspect, resolution and duration pickers, with no frame-rate or audio control found (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:943, :966).
CLI and VS Code: no video mode (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/046-video-generation-studio.md).
prerequisites: Not applicable: nothing to use. Video generation in general needs a signed-in account on a plan that includes video generation (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1001-1012, :1102-1115).
screens_and_controls: No frame-rate control and no audio-upload control exist. A search of apps and packages for frame-rate and reference-audio names found no matches in TypeScript or TSX sources.
journey: A person opens video mode and writes a prompt.
They can set model, aspect ratio, quality and length, but no frame rate or audio file.
They send. The request carries no frame rate or audio reference.
feedback_and_outputs: No related feedback exists. The clip comes back at whatever frame rate the provider chooses; the app never states one [inferred from the absent field].
settings: None. generate_audio is a request field the server accepts but the Web client's request type omits it (apps/web/features/media/services/media-api-service.ts:41-51).

working: The server decides audio on its own: generate_audio defaults to the model's supportsAudio flag, or true for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1207-1208).
The server refuses audio when the model does not support it and refuses audio-off for the google provider (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:469-474).
Generated audio is passed to OpenRouter as generate_audio (apps/web/lib/services/openrouter-video-provider-service.ts:147).
incomplete: The model catalog describes video models with durations, output sizes, audio support and seed support only; there is no frame-rate field (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:213-219).
disconnected_or_disabled: generate_audio exists in the shared request schema (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:199) but no app UI sends it (media-api-service.ts:41-51; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:126; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:610-613).
not_available: Frame-rate selector: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Reference-audio input: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome.
Both: CLI and VS Code (no video mode).

established.statement: A person picks the frame rate of the clip where the model supports it.
A person supplies reference audio (voice or music) for the clip where supported.
Advertised video options must produce real decodable media, and unsupported configurations must show an honest disabled state.

acceptance_criteria: When a video model declares supported frame rates, the composer shows a frame-rate control listing only those rates; models that declare none show no control.
The generate request carries the chosen frame rate and the server rejects a rate the model does not list, in the same way it rejects an unsupported duration (route.ts:446-481 pattern).
A model that accepts reference audio shows an audio attach control; a model that does not shows it disabled with a reason.
Reference audio is validated for type and size before upload and is covered by the same content-safety checks as prompts and images.
The cost estimate (VideoCostEstimate) reflects any price change caused by the chosen options.
Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome offer the same control or an honest disabled state; none shows a dead control.
inferred: A frame-rate field would need to be added to the catalog model description first, because the server validates duration and size against the catalog (route.ts:446-481) [inferred].
Reference audio would need a new uploaded-file type, since reference images today are image-only (managed-media.ts:209-216) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add optional frame_rates and supports_reference_audio to the video metadata in the model catalog, edit the curation file and regenerate, and read them in the composer.
[proposed] Keep generate_audio as the single audio on/off switch and add a separate reference-audio input only for models that declare it.

steps.what_happens: The person writes a prompt and sets model, aspect ratio, quality and length in the video composer; no frame-rate or audio file step exists.
The client posts prompt, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, model and optional images to the Cloud route.

The server validates the body against the shared schema (unknown fields are rejected because the schema is strict), then resolves audio, checks model limits, billing allowance and starts a durable job.
The job calls the video provider (Runway, Google or OpenRouter) with the chosen model; frame rate and audio reference are never sent.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Model choice is read from the model catalog. Frame-rate support and reference-audio support are not described in the catalog today, so no model can be offered them. Providers on the managed video path are runway, google and openrouter (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:358); only google and openrouter have a folder under packages/ai/providers.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in AGI account (Clerk-based) is required for the Cloud video route; Chrome shows 'Sign in to your AGI account to create videos.' (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/videoGenerationClient.ts:97-103). No account rule specific to frame rate or audio reference exists.
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy, model policy and spend-limit gates run before billing (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:925-945). None specific to this feature.
access_and_usage.subscription: Video generation is limited to the plans listed by billing capability video_generation (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357). Frame rate and audio reference have no separate entitlement because they do not exist.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Video is metered in video_seconds units (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1239-1246). Nothing priced by frame rate or reference audio.
access_and_usage.flags: capability canUseVideoGeneration gates the route (route.ts:1011). No flag for these items.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable until the catalog carries the fields. supportsAudio exists per model (model-catalog.ts:216).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The google provider generates audio with every video and refuses audio-off (route.ts:472-474). Whether any provider API accepts frame rate or reference audio: unknown, not checked.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Video generation runs only in Cloud. No Local video path was found in the video route or the Desktop and Mobile clients read; Mobile asks cloud-send consent first (apps/mobile/src/features/video/services/videogen.ts:97). Local-mode video: none found in the code.

missing_facts: Video generation needs the max_15x or enterprise plan: packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:357. The page never says which plans, and an account with no subscription gets 'No active subscription found' (route.ts:1102-1115).

Candidate count n (1 to MANAGED_MEDIA_MAX_VIDEO_CANDIDATES) makes one durable job and one billed reservation per candidate, so metered video_seconds scale with n (managed-media.ts:204; route.ts:1239-1246).

Runway has its own prompt cap of 1,000 characters (route.ts:1209-1210) and its own path (generateWithRunway). The page says nothing about it, though it is an audio and option difference between providers.
